distractors.reason: 'Good' is an adjective. After a verb we need an adverb, so we say 'play well', not 'play good'.
'Quick' is an adjective. We do not say 'play quick'; the adverb form is 'quickly', and it describes speed, not skill.
'Happy' is an adjective for feelings. It does not describe how someone plays in this sense.

example_sentence: Sam can play ___ with the new board game.
l1_interference: Falantes de português podem traduzir 'jogar bem' como 'play good'. Em inglês, usa-se o advérbio 'well' depois do verbo, e não o adjetivo 'good'.
explanation: In English, verb + adverb collocations use an adverb to describe how an action is done. 'Well' is the adverb used with 'play' when you mean doing it skillfully.

related_collocations.example: Kids should sleep well at night.
Please listen carefully to the rules of the game.

memory_tip: PLAY + WELL = do it skillfully | 'good' is an adjective and never goes after play
